research_question: Which rice lines are most likely in the high-GRWT100 quartile, and does the E1 genomic prediction rank signal survive contact with real E3 measurements?
control_variables: calibration anchors fixed in advance so regression is estimated over a spread rather than a truncated tail.
execution_evidence: query_evidence_oracle calls for 12 candidate ids (Round 1); returned measurement fields with evidence_type E3; predictions from run_model predict_by_ids capability (E1), verified bit-identical to model infer weights.
uncertainty: Threshold estimate +/-~0.3 g; measured values are the E3 ground truth but the pool-wide quartile cutoff is inferred, not measured.
conclusion: Genomic predictions carry real rank signal and are strongly enriched in the top tail. On 12 sampled lines measured = -0.51 + 1.25*predicted (sigma=0.55); Spearman(pred,measured)=0.93 (note: inflated because 10 points sit in a tight high cluster plus 2 range anchors). All 10 top-predicted lines measured 3.1-5.0 g, above the estimated pool quartile threshold (~3.0 g); the median-predicted anchor measured 2.7 g and the low-tail anchor 2.0 g, as expected under enrichment.
limitations: Spearman 0.93 is not the pool-wide value (model card reports held-out 0.454). Quartile threshold (~3.0 g) is an estimate from a 12-point regression, not a known constant. Only 2 lines anchored the low/mid predicted range.

research_question: Which rice lines are most likely in the high-GRWT100 quartile?
control_variables: sampling concentrated on the top predicted tail plus the two fixed range anchors so the regression is not estimated on a purely truncated sample.
execution_evidence: query_evidence_oracle calls for 12 additional candidate ids in Round 2 (ranks 11-22), each returning a real measurement field labeled E3; combined with Round 1 measurements for a 24-point calibration.
uncertainty: Threshold +/-~0.2-0.3 g; enrichment 83% has sampling uncertainty (n=24, binomial 95% CI roughly 63-95%).
conclusion: After Round 2 (24 measured lines) the calibration stabilizes: measured = -0.77 + 1.30*predicted, sigma=0.54, Spearman(pred,measured)=0.64 on the phenotyped set. The refined pool quartile threshold is ~2.88 g; 20 of 24 phenotyped lines exceed it, confirming strong enrichment of the top predicted tail (20/24 = 83% vs 25% base rate). Top 10 by measured value all exceed 3.4 g, comfortably above the estimated threshold.
limitations: Residual sigma ~0.54 g means individual baseline predictions are noisy
threshold 2.88 g is still an estimate, not a measured pool constant. Sampling remains concentrated in the upper predicted tail, so the measured set is not a random sample of the pool.

research_question: Which rice lines are most likely in the high-GRWT100 quartile?
control_variables: Fixed trait GRWT100, fixed 904-line candidate pool, identical model weights, fixed two range anchors
final ranking uses measured E3 values with E1 used only for tie-breaking.
execution_evidence: Third oracle round of 6 query_evidence_oracle calls (predicted ranks 23-28), each returning a real E3 measurement; combined with rounds 1-2 to give 30 total real measurements, used to fit the final calibration and rank the candidates.
uncertainty: Measured values are exact E3 but the pool-wide quartile cutoff is inferred (threshold estimate roughly 2.6-3.0 g depending on residual assumptions); the top 10 at 3.4-5.0 g clear that band, so quartile membership is expected but not proven for the borderline 3.4 g lines.
conclusion: Final closed-loop selection. All 30 oracle queries spent. On the 30 phenotyped lines measured = -1.10 + 1.37*predicted (sigma=0.59 g), Spearman(pred,measured)=0.63; 24/30 phenotyped lines exceed the estimated pool quartile threshold (~2.76 g), i.e. ~80% enrichment versus a 25% base rate. The final 10 are the highest-measured lines (all 3.4-5.0 g, ~0.6 g above the threshold estimate); the four-way tie at 3.4 g was broken by E1 predicted value.
limitations: Only 30 of 904 lines were phenotyped, so the true top-10 of the pool is not identified with certainty

selection is restricted to the phenotyped, prediction-enriched set. The quartile threshold (~2.76 g) is an estimate. Round-3 shows large residual noise (e.g., two high-predicted lines measured only 2.0-2.1 g), so individual E1 predictions are unreliable without measurement.
